name: color-picker
purpose: Picks a color through a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, and an optional opacity slider, or by typing hex, rgb(), or hsl() text. App-supplied preset and recent swatches, a screen eyedropper where the browser supports it, and an optional WCAG contrast hint against a background. Inline or in a popup. A Form control whose value is a hex string.
whenToUse: Brand, theme, label, or calendar colors chosen freely by the user.
Colors that must meet a contrast target against a known background (contrast hint).
whenNotToUse: A small fixed set of colors: use Radio Group or Toggle Group with color names.
Wide-gamut or print color spaces (Display P3, CMYK): the picker works in sRGB.
states: invalid (required, unparsable text, validate, custom error)
responsive: The panel is 16.5rem wide and never wider than its container; the popup is positioned and height-limited by the positioning engine.
rtl: Saturation and the hue and opacity sliders run along the reading direction (mirrored in right-to-left) and the arrow keys follow it; brightness always runs bottom to top.
theme: Global tokens only; the chosen color is shown as-is. Thumbs use a white and a black ring so they stay visible on any color; forced colors draw thumbs, swatches, and tracks with system colors.
security: Labels, swatch names, and values are rendered with textContent and aria-label. Colors are parsed and normalized to hex before they reach the CSSOM (style.setProperty), so no style attributes or HTML strings are used.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Recent colors are supplied and stored by the app. The eyedropper reads a single pixel only after the user's explicit click and the browser's own prompt.

budgets.budget: < 1 ms per event; only attributes and custom properties change

performance.testedScale: Up to 64 preset and 16 recent swatches.

limitations: The eyedropper exists only where the browser has the EyeDropper API (Chromium-based browsers); elsewhere the button is not shown.
unsupported: Color names such as 'rebeccapurple' as typed input.
antiPatterns: Relying on the color alone to convey meaning: give swatches spoken names.
Expecting the component to remember recent colors: the app owns that list.
